title: Q4 Exec Iteration Playbook and Comms
body:
Purpose:
This doc is a lightweight playbook for the Q4 company-wide sync we want to run as an ‘exec iteration’ rather than a classic all-hands. Goal: align the org around the updated OKR surface, highlight decisions since the midyear reset, and trigger the Dedicated/Private GTM cadence.

Audience:
- All employees (primary)
- Leadership + execs (secondary)
- Customer-facing teams for comms lift-off

High-level narrative (one-sentence):
We will show the measurable progress on production inference SLAs, outline the product rollout timeline for Dedicated capacity expansion, and set three operational priorities for the next 90 days (cost/perf, rollouts, enterprise readiness).

Proposed draft OKRs (short, numeric targets) - WORKING DRAFT:
- OKR 1 (Product/Serving): Increase 95th percentile API latency SLA compliance to 99% across hosted clusters by EOD Q4. (KR1.1 reduce p95 by 20ms on average; KR1.2 adopt two additional kernel-level optimizations)
- OKR 2 (Go-to-market): Close 10 Dedicated contracts (monthly reserved capacity >= $50k) with three enterprise pilots in regulated sectors.
- OKR 3 (Cost & Efficiency): Reduce per-token infra cost for production workload by 18% via batching/quantization profiles and autoscaling policy changes.
- OKR 4 (Reliability/Compliance): Complete SOC2 re-audit gap remediation and ship Private beta with KMS integration to 2 customers.
(Notes: metrics shown below are snapshots; KRs will get owner assignments in the next PR)

Top-line metrics snapshot (to show on slides):
- Monthly tokens (hosted): 18.4B (↑ 12% vs prior quarter)
- Avg p95 latency (hosted API): 320ms
- Production inference cost per 1k tokens: $0.42
- Dedicated revenue MRR: $420k
- Trial Private customers in pipeline: 6 (2 in legal review)

Run of show (45-50m total):
- 0:00–0:05 Welcome + framing (CEO) - state of the company in 2 slides
- 0:05–0:15 Product highlights (Head of Serving Runtime) - concrete wins + cost/latency charts
- 0:15–0:25 GTM & Enterprise progress (Head of Sales) - Dedicated deals and pilot stories
- 0:25–0:35 Ops & Reliability playbook (SRE lead) - rollout/canary plan, fallback policies
- 0:35–0:45 OKR refresh & what we expect from teams (Head of Product) - calls to action
- 0:45–0:50 Close + 2 live Qs + where to find follow-ups (Comms lead)

Speaker notes / storyline bullets (do not read every bullet):
CEO: start with one short example customer problem that would have failed without our fallbacks; emphasize serving as the moat.
Serving Runtime: show before/after p95 reduction with kernel change X, include a micro-graph of cost delta per 1k tokens. Call out remaining risks: tail latencies on long-context workloads.
GTM: highlight three enterprise pilots (anonymized): fintech, health, large-SaaS. Ask product for a single handoff checklist for pilots -> Dedicated onboarding.
SRE: show canary runbook steps and the auto-fallback flow (hosted -> dedicated -> private). Note: keep this high-level; the deep runbook lives in SRE Confluence link.
Product: summarize OKR lines and ask each eng/product team to confirm owner and top 2 signals for KR measurement within one week.

Prep checklist (owner):
- Final slides due: 2026-03-15 (Aisha Patel)
- Metrics slide (single source of truth): Diego to pull from metrics-dashboard -> final csv by 2026-03-12
- Dedicated pilot one-pagers collected: Priya to collate by 2026-03-13
- Confluence update with OKR detail + KR owners: Michael (me) to create page 2026-03-11
- Q&A backlog: collect via #company-questions -> close top 10 before live

Audience engagement plan:
- Live poll (two questions): which KR will your team need cross-functional help on? and which pilot do you want to join the tap-in?
- Post-sync survey (2 minutes) with 3 asks: confirm owner, identify blockers, opt-in for pilot help.
- Record session + publish short 3-slide summary + action list in Slack within 24 hours.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Metric mismatch between dashboards -> Mitigation: single metrics owner (Diego) + freeze for slides at T-48h.
- Risk: Sales asks overwhelm engineering -> Mitigation: Product to gate with pilot checklist and commit to SLO for onboarding capacity.
- Risk: Exec time overruns -> Mitigation: strict run-of-show and hard stop at 50m; follow-up office hours scheduled.

Open questions / decisions needed before finalize (short):
- Do we want to publish the Dedicated pricing tiers during the sync or wait until next week? (tradeoff: better transparency vs. premature public commitment)
- Are we comfortable moving the Private beta milestone from KR4 M2 to M1 (accelerate)? This requires 2x effort from infra in the next 30 days.
- Approve the three “operational priorities” that teams will be asked to commit resources to for next 90 days.

Action items (first pass):
- Michael: publish Confluence page and assign initial KR owners (due 2026-03-11).
- Aisha: finalize slides + host rehearsal (2026-03-15).
- Diego: deliver metric snapshot CSV and pick canonical visualization (2026-03-12).
- Priya: collect pilot one-pagers + readiness checklist (2026-03-13).

Notes to self / reminders (messy):
- Keep the ‘production-first’ story front and center; engineering audience responds better to concrete performance numbers than marketing language.
- Save 3 minutes at the end for a specific ask: teams to pick 1 KR to escalate if they need cross-team help.
- Add a short appendix slide with SLO definitions and fallback policy summary.

References / links for slides:
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/TEAM-Q4-STRATEGY
- Metrics dashboard (internal): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/q4-deck
- JIRA epic for pilot onboarding: RW-PLANNING-Q4-42

Status: draft — seeking feedback from execs (please add comments in the Confluence page or Slack thread).

End of doc.
